description:
[Interviews] Update the configuration of an existing interview/position: name, description, avatar template, recording, scoring, tags, category and the rest of the create-time settings; for a position also its hiring `team` and recruiter. `status` is applied as set_interview_state applies it (archiving an active position can e-mail its open applicants; set_interview_state with dry_run previews that); the vacancy lifecycle and the embed key are set with set_interview_state only. A position's steps are changed with set_position_process and update_position_step. Only the fields you send are changed. To change the questions, send `questions` — the WHOLE list you want the interview to end up with, in order, in the format get_interview_definition returns. OMIT `questions` and the existing questions are left completely alone; there is no way to change one question on its own: the array get_interview_definition returns is edited and sent back whole. Resending an unchanged array does nothing. On an offline (pre-rendered video) template the questions change only while the interview is `draft`; on an interactive one also while it is `active`. Not updated by this tool at all: the welcome and thank-you messages and the instructional-video screen (stored as steps, not questions), and the language, which the existing questions are already written in (no tool changes these: the messages and the video screen are changed in the admin, and another language takes a new interview). `tags` places a coaching session into a catalogue directory. MULTI-STAGE POSITIONS: the interview-only settings (recording, knowledge_base_store_id, candidate_expectations_json and the like) do not exist at position level and are refused with a 422 naming the field. They live on the AI interview step's own interview (the step's interview_set_id, from get_interview_definition include=process). A null argument counts as not sent and changes nothing, except on three fields where null is the only way to switch something off: `candidate_notification_channel` (no SMS / WhatsApp), `questions_random_subset` (ask all questions) and `pdf_export_auto_config` (no automatic report).

Every argument in full, with examples: get_tool_reference.

allow_human_interview.description: A recruiter may hold the interview instead of the AI. Single-stage interviews only (an interview step of a position carries its own setting, see update_position_step).

candidate_expectations_json.description: Structured candidate expectations (the scoring rubric), bucketed by requirement level (weak/moderate/strong). A null is ignored: send a new rubric to replace it, or regenerate_candidate_expectations together with `questions` to derive it again.

candidate_notification_channel.description: SMS / WhatsApp notifications to the candidate, sent alongside the e-mails: "reminders" = with both e-mail reminders (day 1 and day 3); "last_reminder" = only with the final day-3 reminder; "all" = invitation, both reminders and the pre-screening-accepted step. null switches them off.

candidate_video_introduction.description: Whether a candidate video introduction is hidden, optional or required. Send `hidden` to stop asking.

coach_plan.description: Coaching-plan stage this item belongs to, used by the coaching-plan progress view. Omit to keep the current stage. A null is ignored: use `other` when no stage fits. Values: `demo`: Demo session | `screening`: Screening-interview practice | `2nd`: Second-interview practice | `3rd`: Third-interview practice | `closing`: Closing / salary-negotiation practice | `job-specific`: Job-specific coaching | `other`: Anything that does not fit the other buckets.

code.description: External code/reference. Blank is stored as null.

collect_resume_cover_letter.description: Ask the candidate for a resume / cover letter: hidden, optional or required. Single-stage interviews only.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id this server returned earlier in this conversation, unchanged, including after later user messages. Omit it if you have none. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

country_availability.description: Which countries the interview / position is open to on the candidate portal, judged by the IP address the candidate opens it from (an unknown location only passes when countries_allowed / countries_allowed_eu are empty). From a closed country it is left out of the portal listings, and a direct link shows "not available in your region". Invited candidates (personal invitation links) and candidates who already started keep access; API and MCP calls themselves are never restricted. An empty object {} = not used, every country.

custom_fields.description: Company-defined position fields to set, {key: value}; a null value clears that field and keys you omit keep their value. Requires custom fields to be enabled for the company (else 403). Multi-stage positions only: on a single-stage interview the request is refused with 422.

custom_scoring.description: Result-scoring overrides (max_score, early_stop, speech_cadence, ai_pronunciation, sentiment_analysis, ai_assessment_answer, ai_assessment_resume, ai_assessment_session). Merged onto the stored configuration, so keys you omit keep their current value.

emoji.description: Emoji marker shown in the admin lists. Blank is stored as null.

environment.description: Which of your webhook environments results from this interview are delivered to. Defaults to production. Values: `production`: Live hiring | `uat`: User-acceptance testing - an isolated environment for pre-release verification | `development`: Development/testing | `demo`: Demonstrations and sales trials.

hiring_for_company.description: Who the position is really for. An object with name null/blank means hiring for yourself; { name: 'undisclosed' } for an unnamed external client; or { name: '<company>' } plus optional description/location/sector/company_size.

interview_available_till.description: ISO date/time after which the interview is no longer available to candidates. An empty string makes it always available.

interview_category.description: Job category shown on public listings above the department (free text), e.g. "Ashore". Blank is stored as null.

interview_conversation_speed.description: Conversation pace of the AI avatar. Omit to keep the current pace; `normal` is the default speaking pace. Values: `slower`: The avatar speaks more slowly | `normal`: Default speaking pace | `faster`: The avatar speaks more quickly for a snappier conversation | `fluent`: Talking pace: the avatar answers 300 ms after the candidate stops speaking.

interview_department.description: Department the position belongs to. Blank is stored as null.

interview_salary.description: Salary range shown for the position. Blank is stored as null.

interview_template_id.description: Id of the interview template (avatar/voice) to use.

interview_tone.description: Tone — configures the AI avatar's speaking style and the follow-up questions it generates. Case-insensitive; omit to keep the current tone. Values: `relaxed`: Friendly and conversational tone that helps candidates feel at ease | `simple`: Plain language at CEFR A2 level | `professional`: Formal and business-like approach suitable for senior roles | `persuasive`: Engaging style that encourages candidates to elaborate | `exact`: Asks the questions exactly as provided, without rephrasing.

interview_type.description: Interview style — configures the AI avatar and the follow-up questions it generates during the interview. Values: `pre-screening`: quick qualification check focusing on basic requirements and availability | `pre-screening-with-test-questions`: pre-screening plus practical questions to test relevant skills | `second-interview`: deeper dive for candidates who passed initial screening | `remote-freelancer-verification`: verify remote work capabilities and communication skills | `strength-based-interview`: focus on what candidates enjoy and excel at to predict job satisfaction | `potential-based-interview`: assess learning ability and growth potential rather than past experience | `process-verification-from-knowledge-base`: generate questions from your knowledge base documents | `knockout-screening`: a short (about 5 minute) check of the role's must-haves with closed questions.

knowledge_base_store_id.description: Knowledge base store id the interview draws context from; validated for existence. An empty string unlinks it.

llm_model.description: Your model id, e.g. "claude-opus-4-8"; "unknown" if unsure. For analytics.

location.description: Interview location. Blank is stored as null.

max_followups.description: Maximum number of AI follow-up questions. 0 disables follow-ups; presets are 0-3 (none/low/normal/high) and custom values start at 4; 2 is the template default (Normal).

pdf_export_auto_config.description: Auto-generate a candidate PDF report with these options once the interview completes. null disables auto-export.

position_id.description: Id of the interview definition (single-stage) or position definition (multi-stage) to update.

questions.description: OPTIONAL. Omit this field entirely and the interview's questions are left exactly as they are — questions are only touched when you send the array. When sent, it is the COMPLETE list you want the interview to end up with, in order, in the same format create_interview accepts and get_interview_definition returns: there is no way to change a single question on its own: the array get_interview_definition returns is edited and sent back whole. An empty array is rejected. It is applied as a DIFF, not a replace, so resending the array get_interview_definition gave you changes nothing at all. Each entry is matched against what is stored — first on `external_id`, then on `id`, then on identical content — and: an entry matching an unchanged question keeps that question exactly as it is, including its answer rules and any rendered avatar video; an entry matching a question whose content differs unlinks the old question and creates a new one in its place (fields you omit are carried over from the old one); an entry matching nothing is created; and a stored question no entry matches is unlinked. Questions are shared records, so nothing is ever deleted — removing one only unlinks it from this interview, and an edit is always unlink-old + create-new so the change cannot leak into another interview reusing the same question. Single-stage interviews only; a multi-stage position's interview stages are updated individually.

questions_random_subset.description: Ask only a random subset of the questions, as a fraction between 0.01 and 0.9. null asks all questions.

recording.description: Cheating/proctoring detection mode for candidate answers — this is NOT a full session recording. Omit to keep the current mode; `none` switches it off; a null is ignored. Values: `audio_first_5_answers`: Audio-only cheating detection, first 5 answers only | `audio_all`: Audio-only cheating detection on every answer | `video_all`: Audio + video cheating detection on every answer | `video_first_5_answers`: Audio + video cheating detection, first 5 answers only | `none`: Switch cheating detection off.

recording_full_session.description: Full interview-session recording (includes the avatar and voice) produced as a single file. Omit to keep the current setting; `none` switches it off; a null is ignored. Values: `audio_all`: Record the whole session audio | `video_all`: Record the whole session video + audio | `none`: Switch the full-session recording off.

recruiter_profile_id.description: Profile id of the recruiter owning this interview or position (`profile_id` (list_users)). Must be an active owner, recruiter or admin of the company (own staff or a sub-merchant grant holder), else 422. An empty string clears it.

regenerate_candidate_expectations.description: Re-derive the interview-level `candidate_expectations_json` scoring rubric from the resulting question list, the way create_interview derives it at creation time. Only applies when `questions` is sent, the interview type is `interview`, and `candidate_expectations_json` is not also being set explicitly (an explicit value wins).

required_pronunciation.description: Require pronunciation assessment (restricts to pronunciation-capable languages).

result_enable_edit_transcript.description: Allow editing the transcript on the result view.

result_view.description: Result screen shown to the candidate after finishing. With any value other than `none`, the candidate sees a results screen where they can provide feedback, record an intro video and edit the transcript, and must then submit the result; the value sets how much score/result detail is shown. Values: `none`: No results screen at all | `minimal`: Minimal results layout, no score shown | `minimal_with_score`: Minimal results layout including the overall score | `advanced`: Advanced results layout with more detail | `full`: Full results layout with all sections | `full_expand_scores`: Full results with every score breakdown expanded.

seniority_level.description: Target seniority level for the role; omit to keep the current one. Values: `entry-level`: Early-career or graduate roles | `intermediate`: Some experience required | `senior`: Experienced professional | `managerial`: Team or department lead | `director`: Director-level responsibility | `executive`: C-suite or executive role.

status.description: New publication status (preparing and completed are normally set by the platform), applied exactly as set_interview_state applies it: archiving an active position e-mails its candidates with open applications when the position-closed notice is on (set_interview_state previews that with dry_run, and also manages the iframe embed key and the vacancy lifecycle of a position). Refused (422) for the AI interview step of a multi-stage position: its status follows the position.

tags.description: Free-form tags stored on the interview. Only `active` sessions with visibility `merchant_public` (or the platform's own `public`) are listed.

team.description: Multi-stage positions only (422 on an interview): the complete hiring team you want, replacing the current members (viewers, managed with position access, are kept). An empty array removes everyone. Needs the hiring team switched on for the company (else 403) and access to the position.

type.description: Product type of the interview. Changing it also re-derives `type_credit` (null for interview/assessment, otherwise interview_coach_manager) unless you send `type_credit` explicitly. Single-stage interviews only.

type_credit.description: Credit bucket the session draws from. Only meaningful for candidate-paid coaching/persona sessions; hiring interviews and assessments are merchant-billed and carry null. Values: `resume_check`: Resume Builder credits | `interview_coach_starter`: starter tier | `interview_coach_contributor`: contributor tier | `interview_coach_manager`: manager tier | `cover_letter`: Cover-letter credits.

visibility.description: Who can discover and access the interview. Refused (422) for the AI interview step of a multi-stage position: it follows the position. Values: `merchant_public`: Listed on the merchant's public interview list | `merchant_invite`: only candidates explicitly invited | `merchant_unlisted`: Reachable only via a direct link.

name: update_interview
title: Update interview or position
